Why it's a good choice for flying

Airline-friendly capacity: At approximately 74 Wh, it's under the FAA's 100 Wh threshold for spare lithium-ion batteries.

Versatile charging: The 100 W output can charge compatible laptops as well as phones and tablets.

Convenient design: The flat form factor and digital battery display are useful when traveling.

Important airplane rules

According to the FAA's passenger battery guidance:

Carry it in the cabin. Power banks are not permitted in checked baggage.

Keep it accessible. If your carry-on is gate-checked, remove the power bank and keep it with you in the cabin.

Check your airline's policy. Airlines can impose stricter limits than the general FAA rules.

Avoid damaged batteries. Don't travel with a damaged or recalled power bank.

One important caveat: Southwest's supplied policy says that, effective April 20, 2026, each passenger may bring only one power bank, which must be 100 Wh or less, stored in a personal item under the seat, and not charged using in-seat power. Other airlines may have different requirements. Check Southwest's current policy.

My verdict

I'd choose the Baseus Blade H1 if you want one power bank for your phone and laptop. Its 20,000 mAh capacity and 100 W output make it a capable travel option while staying below the FAA's standard 100 Wh threshold.

If you're only charging a phone, a smaller, lighter power bank may be more convenient. If you're bringing a laptop, this Baseus is the stronger all-around choice from the products in your supplied results.
